key_insight: CLExEval shows that fluent LLM clinical reasoning can look convincing while still missing the correct diagnosis, especially when information is scarce or masked.
clinical_relevance: The study warns that automated medical evaluations may overestimate real-world clinical reliability unless expert-reviewed reasoning is included.
method: Human-in-the-loop evaluation with progressive information masking
5,600 expert-physician annotations across 200 reasoning traces from 40 rare diagnostic cases
Comparison of model outputs against human-verified failure cases and LLM-as-a-Judge scoring
evidence_signal: In the abstract, GPT-4o-mini’s diagnostic accuracy fell from 95.0% to 32.5% under scarcity, and judges approved 47.9% of clinically incorrect outputs.
watch_item: Results come from rare-case traces and judge behavior, so broader clinical settings and deployment workflows may not generalize directly.
paper_title: CLExEval: A Human-in-the-Loop Framework for Qualitative Evaluation of LLM Clinical Reasoning
